title: Breathlessness in a 68-year-old retired bus driver
intended_learner: Medical students and first-year emergency medicine residents
unknown_response: I'm not sure. I can't really tell you anything about that.
prebrief: You are the emergency medicine resident. Leonard Asante, 68, has been brought in by his daughter with worsening breathlessness. Triage has started oxygen. Take a history, request the examination and tests you need, find out why he has got worse, and decide on a disposition.

profile.name: Leonard Asante
profile.background: Retired city bus driver, widowed 14 months ago, lives alone on the second floor.
profile.personality: Dignified, private, dry sense of humour; embarrassed by anything to do with the bathroom.
profile.speech_style: Unhurried, short of breath, pauses between phrases. Understates.

faculty_truth.diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure precipitated by stopping furosemide, anti-inflammatory painkiller use and high salt intake
teaching_points: Finding the reason for a decompensation (medicines stopped, new medicines, diet) is as important as recognising it.
A dispensing record can show a gap the patient is embarrassed to admit; raise it kindly and ask what got in the way.
Over-the-counter anti-inflammatory painkillers are a common, easily missed precipitant.
Bereavement and low mood undermine self-care routines such as daily weights.

facts.statement: Worsening shortness of breath over two weeks, much worse for three days
facts.patient_answer: I can't get my breath. It's been building for a couple of weeks, and the last three days it's been bad.

facts.statement: Used to walk four blocks to the shop; now stops after half a block and after one flight of stairs
facts.patient_answer: I used to walk four blocks to the store without thinking. Now I stop after half a block. One flight of stairs and I'm done.

facts.statement: Sleeps propped on three pillows; wakes at night gasping and has to sit on the edge of the bed
facts.patient_answer: I'm sleeping on three pillows now. A couple of nights I woke up gasping and had to sit on the edge of the bed.

facts.statement: Both ankles swollen for a week, shoes tight; gained about 4 kg in two weeks
facts.patient_answer: Both ankles are swollen. My shoes are tight. The bathroom scale says I'm up about four kilos in two weeks.

facts.statement: Dry cough at night; no fever; no coloured sputum or blood
facts.patient_answer: A dry cough at night. No fever. Nothing coming up, no blood.

facts.statement: No chest pain, palpitations or fainting
facts.patient_answer: No chest pain. No racing heart. I haven't passed out.

facts.statement: Reduced appetite, feels full after a few bites
facts.patient_answer: I'm not eating much. A few bites and I feel full.

facts.statement: Heart failure diagnosed three years ago after a heart attack; one admission for fluid overload last winter
facts.patient_answer: I had a heart attack three years ago and they told me my heart was weak after it. I was in hospital last winter with fluid on my lungs.

facts.statement: High blood pressure for 15 years; type 2 diabetes for 8 years; no lung disease
facts.patient_answer: High blood pressure for about fifteen years. Diabetes for eight. My lungs have always been fine.

facts.statement: Prescribed furosemide 40 mg each morning, lisinopril 10 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, metformin 500 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg
facts.patient_answer: I'm on a water pill, furosemide. Lisinopril, metoprolol, metformin twice a day, and a cholesterol pill, atorvastatin.

facts.statement: Has taken naproxen twice a day for two weeks for knee pain
facts.patient_answer: I've been taking naproxen for my knee. Twice a day, for a couple of weeks now.

facts.statement: No known drug allergies
Stopped furosemide about three weeks ago: it made him get up to urinate several times a night and he had an accident on the bus; he has not collected a refill
facts.patient_answer: All right. I stopped the water pill about three weeks ago. I was up all night to the bathroom, and I had an accident on the bus. I was too embarrassed to say. I haven't picked up the refill.
facts.cover_answer: I take my pills every morning, same as always.

facts.statement: Eats canned soup and deli meat most days since his wife died; does not limit salt or fluids
facts.patient_answer: Since my wife passed I mostly eat canned soup and sandwiches with deli meat. I don't watch the salt, no.

facts.statement: Widowed 14 months ago; lives alone in a second-floor apartment; daughter visits on Sundays
facts.patient_answer: My wife died fourteen months ago. I live on my own, second floor. My daughter comes by on Sundays.

facts.statement: Retired city bus driver
facts.patient_answer: I drove a city bus for thirty-one years. Retired now.

facts.statement: Stopped smoking 12 years ago (30 pack-years); one beer on Sundays
facts.patient_answer: I quit smoking twelve years ago. I smoked a pack a day for thirty years before that. One beer on a Sunday.

facts.statement: Low mood and poor motivation since his wife's death; has stopped weighing himself and going to the seniors' club
facts.patient_answer: Since she died I don't see much point in the routines. I stopped weighing myself, stopped going to the club. Some days I don't get dressed.

facts.statement: Father died of a heart attack at 70; brother has diabetes
facts.patient_answer: My father died of a heart attack at seventy. My brother has diabetes.

facts.statement: SpO2 91% on room air
facts.label: SpO2

facts.statement: Blood pressure 154/92 mmHg
facts.label: Blood pressure

facts.statement: Heart rate 96 beats/min, respiratory rate 24/min, temperature 36.8 C, weight 94 kg (90 kg at clinic two months ago)
Crackles at both lung bases to the mid zones; speaks in short sentences
Raised jugular venous pressure; third heart sound; no murmur
Pitting oedema of both legs to the knees
BNP 1,240 pg/mL (below 100 makes heart failure unlikely)
facts.label: BNP

facts.statement: Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (reference 0.8-1.2; 1.1 two months ago)
facts.label: Creatinine

facts.statement: Chest X-ray: enlarged heart, upper-lobe vascular redistribution, small bilateral pleural effusions; no consolidation

artifacts.title: Triage note
artifacts.content: 68-year-old man brought by his daughter. Short of breath, worse over three days. Speaking in short sentences. Known 'weak heart'. Says he takes all his medicines. Oxygen started at 2 L/min. ESI 2.

artifacts.title: Pharmacy dispensing record (last 3 months)
artifacts.interpretation: Every medicine except furosemide has been collected on time. A 30-day supply dispensed 9 weeks ago means at least 5 weeks without a refill. A dispensing gap does not by itself prove the medicine was not taken; ask.

artifacts.title: Blood results
artifacts.interpretation: Kidney function is worse than two months ago and sodium is low. In this setting consider fluid overload and the recent anti-inflammatory painkiller.

artifacts.title: Chest X-ray (report)
artifacts.content: PA and lateral chest. The heart is enlarged. Upper-lobe vascular redistribution with interstitial markings at both bases. Small bilateral pleural effusions. No focal consolidation. No pneumothorax.
artifacts.interpretation: Appearances of pulmonary venous congestion with small effusions: fluid overload from heart failure rather than pneumonia.

artifacts.title: Cardiology clinic letter (2 months ago)
artifacts.content: Stable heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (35% on last echocardiogram). Weight 90 kg, no oedema. Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. Continue furosemide 40 mg daily, lisinopril, metoprolol. Advised daily weights, to limit salt, and to avoid anti-inflammatory painkillers.
artifacts.interpretation: Baseline two months ago: 4 kg lighter, no oedema, normal creatinine, and explicit advice to avoid anti-inflammatory painkillers.

objectives.criterion: Elicits the pattern of fluid overload: exertional limit, breathlessness lying flat, swelling and weight gain
objectives.evidence_rule: met when all three are elicited
objectives.feedback_missed: Ask how far he can walk, how he sleeps, and about swelling and weight.

objectives.criterion: Establishes the cardiac history and the prescribed medicines
Discovers that he stopped his diuretic, and why
objectives.evidence_rule: met when the patient discloses stopping furosemide; partly when the learner asks about adherence but accepts 'I take my pills'
objectives.feedback_met: You checked the dispensing record, raised the gap kindly, and learned the real barrier: night-time urination and embarrassment.
objectives.feedback_missed: He said he takes everything, yet he is 4 kg heavier. Request the pharmacy record, then say what you see and ask what got in the way.

objectives.criterion: Identifies other precipitants: anti-inflammatory painkillers and a high-salt diet
objectives.feedback_missed: Ask specifically about over-the-counter painkillers and about what he eats.

objectives.criterion: Examines the chest and requests BNP and a chest X-ray
objectives.evidence_rule: met when all three are requested

objectives.criterion: Explores how he has been coping since his wife's death
objectives.evidence_rule: the patient describes his low mood after sustained empathic engagement
objectives.feedback_missed: He mentioned his wife's death in passing. Acknowledge it and ask how he has been managing; it explains the missed routines.

objectives.criterion: Runs a structured interview: introduction, open question first, summary, clear close
objectives.evidence_rule: three of: introduction, early open question, summary, closing

objectives.criterion: Recognises decompensated heart failure needing admission and names the reversible causes
objectives.evidence_rule: disposition is admit, with a summary naming fluid overload and at least one precipitant
